list.title: RAG Document Assistant
list.descProject: A document-grounded assistant built with Next.js, FastAPI and PostgreSQL/pgvector. It extracts text from PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD files, splits it page by page, embeds it with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, then retrieves, LLM-reranks and answers with deduplicated page-level sources through a documented REST API.

description.title: What I built
points: Accepts PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD uploads with a 50 MB limit and explicit format validation.
Preserves exact page numbers during pypdf/python-docx extraction and RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter chunking.
Embeds chunks in batches of 100 with text-embedding-3-small and stores them in a pgvector HNSW cosine index.
Retrieves 20 candidates, reranks them with gpt-4o-mini structured scoring, then sends the top 5 passages to the answer model.
Returns structured answers with deduplicated document, page, excerpt and similarity-score sources; when context is insufficient, the model leaves sources empty and says so.
Exposes /health, document list/upload/delete and /api/chat endpoints with a Next.js 14 chat UI and document selector.

devopsProcess.title: Delivery & checks
steps: Runs PostgreSQL/pgvector, the FastAPI backend and the Next.js frontend as three Docker Compose services.
Creates the vector extension, tables and HNSW index on startup with a bounded psycopg connection pool.
Keeps model choice, chunk size, retrieval depth, reranking, CORS and upload limit in a documented .env template.
Uses Pydantic settings and response schemas so configuration errors and API contracts fail early.
Adds health checks, upload-size validation and explicit 400/413/500 error paths for operational clarity.
Documents local and Docker workflows, curl examples and troubleshooting steps in the repository README.

list.summary: Document-grounded RAG assistant with page-level citations, LLM reranking and a FastAPI + Next.js stack.

list.title: CommunicFlow v2
list.descProject: The upgraded CommunicFlow platform is a multi-tenant collaboration workspace rather than a single chat app. A React/Vite SPA talks to an Express REST API and a separate GraphQL/Socket.IO messenger. Organisation-scoped access, hardened cookie sessions, 2FA, Turnstile, an internal-service key, a governed Drive, recurrence-based events, SLA-backed reclamations, a notification engine and WebRTC call signalling make v2 a production-oriented system.

description.title: What I built
points: Multi-tenant scope resolution with session-level active organisation and super-admin exception handling.
HS512 access/refresh cookies with pinned algorithms, rotation, database revocation, TOTP 2FA, backup codes and Turnstile.
Dedicated messenger service with GraphQL reads/mutations, Socket.IO rooms, presence, typing, read receipts and bounded history pagination.
WebRTC call signalling with STUN and short-lived HMAC TURN credentials, gated by organisation policy and discussion roles.
Governed Drive with access-checked serving, trash/restore/purge, version history, activity trail, tokenised links and ZIP export.
Notification catalogue with preferences, 30-minute grouping, actor self-exclusion, bulk audience inserts and realtime delivery.
Recurrence stored as rules and expanded at read time with a 366-day horizon and 1,500-occurrence cap; reclamations processed by an SLA job.
Default-deny demo mode with a one-hour token and read-only middleware for safe product demonstrations.

devopsProcess.title: Delivery & checks
steps: Deployed three application services behind nginx: React SPA, Express REST API and GraphQL messenger.
Added health checks and a eight-stage Jenkins pipeline with Compose validation, image snapshots, health polling, smoke verification and retained rollback images.
Hardened edge configuration with security headers, TLS, Cloudflare real-IP handling and WebSocket support.
Shared a Redis-backed session cookie between API and messenger while authenticating internal calls with a constant-time key check.
Added scheduled jobs for notification purge, event reminders, reclamation SLA processing and Drive trash purge.
Ran a local CPU-sized Ollama assistant with Redis rate limiting, production-disabled external providers and a FAQ fallback.

citation.name: Janet Williams
citation.citation: Computer science is more than just lines of code. It's the expression of creativity, problem-solving, and building a digital future.

blogList.title: Design Patterns in Practice: SOLID, Testable Architecture

desc.title: Why patterns — and when not to
desc.description: Use patterns to reduce coupling and improve clarity, not as cargo‑cult. Prefer simple composition unless a pattern measurably improves testability or changeability.

desc.title: SOLID and composition first
desc.description: Apply SRP and DIP to keep modules small and replaceable. Compose behaviors via interfaces; isolate I/O at boundaries to enable pure, unit‑testable cores.

desc.title: Dependency Inversion with DI
desc.description: Depend on abstractions. Inject collaborators (factories, strategies, adapters) to swap implementations in tests and production without touching consumers.

desc.title: Selecting patterns pragmatically
desc.description: Prefer Strategy over if/else trees, Adapter to integrate legacy APIs, Factory to centralize creation with validation and caching. Avoid global Singletons.

desc.title: Smells to avoid
desc.description: God objects, deep inheritance, over‑abstraction and premature patterning. Measure impact: fewer defects, simpler diffs, faster reviews.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: Patterns are tools. Start with clear boundaries, enforce interfaces, and document decisions. Fewer surprises, easier onboarding, better uptime.

blogList.title: Angular Performance: Measurable Wins in the Real World

desc.title: Profile before you tune
desc.description: Use Chrome Performance, Lighthouse, and Angular DevTools to locate slow change detection, heavy zones, and chatty network calls.

desc.title: Change detection + rendering
desc.description: Adopt OnPush + `trackBy` for lists, prefer pure pipes, memoize derived state, and split views with `*ngIf` to defer cost.

desc.title: Network and data flow
desc.description: Batch HTTP requests, cache with RxJS `shareReplay`, debounce user input, and stream incremental data for faster First Interaction.

desc.title: Bundles and delivery
desc.description: Lazy‑load routes, leverage standalone components, audit with `source-map-explorer`, and use image compression + HTTP/2.

desc.title: Guardrails
desc.description: Set CI budgets, watch Core Web Vitals, and fail builds on regressions. Performance is a product requirement, not an afterthought.

blogList.title: Modern React: Hooks, Performance and Clean State

desc.title: Design for simplicity
desc.description: Prefer local state with hooks, lift state only when needed, and co‑locate logic with UI. Small components, clear props contracts.

desc.title: Rendering performance
desc.description: Use `memo`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` judiciously; key lists correctly; virtualize large tables; split bundles with dynamic import.

desc.title: Data fetching patterns
desc.description: Stale‑while‑revalidate with SWR/React Query, optimistic updates, and error boundaries for resilient UX.

desc.title: Testing and accessibility
desc.description: Test with React Testing Library (user‑centric). Ship ARIA‑aware components and verify with axe and keyboard navigation.

desc.title: Maintainability
desc.description: Type with TypeScript, enforce ESLint + Prettier, and document props and invariants.

blogList.title: Practical DevOps: CI/CD, Observability, and Reliability

desc.title: Trunk‑based CI/CD
desc.description: Short‑lived branches, automated tests, and canary releases keep deploys boring. Enforce quality gates with coverage and lint checks.

desc.title: Infrastructure as Code
desc.description: Provision reproducibly with Terraform/Pulumi. Version everything; review changes like code; tag releases and roll back fast.

desc.title: Observability that matters
desc.description: Define SLOs, collect RED/USE metrics, add structured logs with correlation IDs, and trace user journeys.

desc.title: Security in the pipeline
desc.description: SAST/DAST, image scanning, SBOMs, and signed artifacts. Least privilege for runners and secrets management.

desc.title: Runbooks and readiness
desc.description: Health checks, graceful shutdown, and documented incident playbooks. Practice failure injection to build confidence.

blogList.title: Effective TypeScript: Types that Scale with Teams

desc.title: Start strict, stay strict
desc.description: Enable `strict` and incremental builds. Prefer explicit types at boundaries; let inference work inside functions.

desc.title: Modeling with unions
desc.description: Use discriminated unions over flags. Encode invariants in the type system and eliminate whole classes of runtime checks.

desc.title: APIs and contracts
desc.description: Define DTOs and use `zod`/`io-ts` for runtime validation. Generate types from schemas to avoid drift.

desc.title: Utilities and generics
desc.description: Leverage utility types (`Partial`, `Pick`, `Extract`) and thoughtful generics for reusable, readable APIs.

desc.title: Tooling
desc.description: ESLint + Prettier + TS path aliases; enforce no‑any, no‑implicit‑any, and unused checks in CI.

blogList.title: Portfolio SEO: Technical Wins that Recruiters Notice

desc.title: Foundation
desc.description: Unique titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, sitemap.xml and robots.txt. Add JSON‑LD (Person, Project) for rich results.

desc.title: Speed and vitals
desc.description: Optimize images, preconnect critical origins, lazy‑load below‑the‑fold, and monitor LCP/CLS/INP in production.

desc.title: Content that signals expertise
desc.description: Write case studies with problem → approach → measurable outcome. Link to code, demos, and metrics.

desc.title: Internationalization
desc.description: Use `hreflang` and consistent slugs across locales. Keep translations accurate and in sync.

desc.title: Tracking and iteration
desc.description: Set up GA4 + Search Console; review queries and improve pages that already rank on page 2.

blogList.title: GraphQL vs REST: Choose by Constraints, Not Hype

desc.title: When REST wins
desc.description: Simple resources, CDN caching, and long‑lived clients. Version via new representations; keep endpoints stable.

desc.title: When GraphQL shines
desc.description: Mobile/low‑latency apps and complex graphs. Fetch exactly what you need; evolve schemas without breaking clients.

desc.title: Performance reality
desc.description: Guard against N+1 with dataloaders; enforce pagination and depth limits; cache persisted queries.

desc.title: Operational concerns
desc.description: Observability, timeouts, and error budgets matter more than style. Document with OpenAPI/SDL and provide examples.

desc.title: Decision rubric
desc.description: Pick the simplest option that meets SLAs. Hybrid backends are common; measure, don’t guess.

blogList.title: Docker Done Right: Small Images, Fast Deploys

desc.title: Build for production
desc.description: Use multi‑stage builds, pin versions, and minimize layers. Add healthchecks and non‑root users.

desc.title: Smaller, safer images
desc.description: Leverage distroless/alpine when appropriate, `.dockerignore` aggressively, and scan images in CI.

desc.title: Local dev ergonomics
desc.description: Compose for services, bind mounts for hot reload, and named volumes for state.

desc.title: Operational tips
desc.description: Expose minimal ports, set resource limits, and emit structured logs. Document run commands for on‑call.

blogList.title: Testing that Prevents Incidents: A Practical Pyramid

desc.title: Test the contract
desc.description: Favor fast unit tests and contract tests at service boundaries. Mock only what you own.

desc.title: Integration > E2E for most cases
desc.description: A few critical E2E flows are enough. Focus on integration tests for realistic coverage with maintainable speed.

desc.title: Data and determinism
desc.description: Use seed data, freeze time, and isolate external effects. Flaky tests destroy trust and velocity.

desc.title: Coverage as a guide
desc.description: Track mutation coverage where possible and require thresholds in CI; quality over raw percentages.

blogList.title: PWAs that Feel Native: Offline‑First by Design

desc.title: Core capabilities
desc.description: Add installability (Web App Manifest), offline caching, and background sync. Respect user prompts; don’t hijack.

desc.title: Caching strategy
desc.description: Precache shell, runtime cache data, and version aggressively. Plan for invalidation and migrations.

desc.title: UX considerations
desc.description: Design explicit offline states, queue writes, and surface sync status. Keep interactions responsive under poor networks.

desc.title: Measuring success
desc.description: Track install rate, offline sessions served, and crash‑free users. Iterate based on real usage.

blogList.title: Secure Authentication: Cookies, OAuth2 + PKCE, 2FA, Turnstile

desc.title: Why this matters
desc.description: Most auth incidents stem from session handling and weak flows, not cryptography. Use a pragmatic design that is secure, scalable, and user‑friendly.

desc.title: Cookie sessions over localStorage
desc.description: Prefer HTTP‑only, Secure, SameSite cookies with short TTL and rotation. Avoid storing tokens in localStorage to reduce XSS token theft risk.

desc.title: OAuth 2.0 + PKCE
desc.description: Use Authorization Code with PKCE for third‑party login (e.g., Google). Enforce exact redirect URIs, narrow scopes, and validate the state parameter.

desc.title: Add Two‑Factor Authentication
desc.description: Start with TOTP and backup codes; add WebAuthn for phishing resistance. Require step‑up auth for sensitive actions (admin, payouts).

desc.title: Block automated abuse
desc.description: Protect signup/login and recovery forms with Cloudflare Turnstile; always verify on the server. Combine with rate limiting and anomaly detection.

desc.title: Production checklist
desc.description: CSRF protection, session rotation, token revocation, rate limits, device/IP reputation, structured logging without secrets, and security tests in CI (OWASP ASVS).

blogList.title: Real‑Time Messaging with GraphQL Subscriptions + Redis

desc.title: Why isolate messaging
desc.description: Real‑time workloads have unique scaling, ordering, and reliability needs. A dedicated microservice improves performance and team velocity.

desc.title: Core architecture
desc.description: GraphQL over HTTP for queries/mutations; Subscriptions (WebSockets) for realtime. Redis Pub/Sub for live fanout; Redis Streams + DB for durable history.

desc.title: Pub/Sub vs Streams
desc.description: Pub/Sub is low latency and ephemeral; Streams are ordered and durable with backpressure and replay. Use both: Streams for persistence, Pub/Sub for online fanout.

desc.title: Backpressure and ordering
desc.description: Persist first, ack after durable write. Use Stream IDs for per‑conversation order and idempotency keys to prevent duplicates.

desc.title: Security and abuse controls
desc.description: Authorize on subscribe/publish, rate‑limit sends, encrypt in transit/at rest, and apply quotas per user/org.

blogList.title: AI Agents in Production: RAG, Guardrails and Cost Control

desc.title: Why agents fail in production
desc.description: Most agent prototypes break on ambiguous intent, stale context, and unbounded tool calls. Treat an agent as a workflow with explicit state, not a magic prompt.

desc.title: RAG that survives real questions
desc.description: Chunk by meaning, keep metadata filters, and rerank before generation. Ground answers in retrieved sources and show citations so users can verify claims.

desc.title: Guardrails and tool boundaries
desc.description: Give each tool a narrow contract, validate inputs with schemas, cap iterations, and require human approval for irreversible actions.

desc.title: Cost and latency control
desc.description: Cache embeddings, route simple turns to smaller models, stream responses, and track tokens per task. A budget is a product constraint, not an afterthought.

desc.title: Evaluation before launch
desc.description: Build an eval set from real support tickets, score groundedness and task success, and replay failures in CI. Model upgrades should be measurable.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: Start with a deterministic workflow, add retrieval where context matters, and only then add autonomy. Observability turns a demo into a dependable feature.

blogList.title: Platform Engineering in 2026: Build an Internal Developer Platform

desc.title: Why platforms replace ticket ops
desc.description: When every team assembles its own pipeline, delivery slows and security becomes inconsistent. A platform turns repeated setup into a self-service product.

desc.title: Start with the golden path
desc.description: Publish opinionated templates for services, jobs, and infrastructure. A new repository should ship a tested app with observability and policy already wired in.

desc.title: Idempotent infrastructure
desc.description: Use Terraform or Pulumi modules with versioned interfaces. Expose environments through a catalog, never through hand-edited consoles.

desc.title: Measure developer experience
desc.description: Track lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate and recovery time. Ask developers where they wait; remove that step first.

desc.title: Avoid the platform trap
desc.description: Do not build a ticket queue with a UI. Keep escape hatches, document ownership, and treat the platform like any other product with a roadmap.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: A good IDP reduces cognitive load, not choice. Standardize the boring parts and let teams innovate where it matters.

blogList.title: Software Supply Chain Security: SBOM, Signing and Zero Trust CI

desc.title: The attack surface is the build
desc.description: Dependencies, runners, and release artefacts are now primary targets. Lock the path from source to production with verified steps.

desc.title: Generate an SBOM by default
desc.description: Produce CycloneDX or SPDX in every build. Store it with the release so you can answer 'are we affected?' in minutes, not days.

desc.title: Sign and verify artefacts
desc.description: Use Sigstore or cosign to sign images and packages. Admission policies should reject anything without a valid signature and provenance.

desc.title: Harden CI runners
desc.description: Use short-lived tokens, least-privilege roles, pinned actions, and isolated builds. Never place long-lived secrets in a shared runner.

desc.title: Patch with evidence
desc.description: Pair dependency scanning with reachability analysis and a clear SLA. Auto-merge low-risk updates, review breaking ones, and record exceptions.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: Supply chain security is not a scanner. It is a chain of verifiable claims: what you built, from what, and who approved it.

blogList.title: Core Web Vitals in 2026: Master INP, LCP and Real User Monitoring

desc.title: Lab scores are not enough
desc.description: Lighthouse is useful for debugging, but search ranking and user experience depend on field data. Instrument real users with the web-vitals library.

desc.title: Fix INP at the interaction
desc.description: Break long tasks, yield to the main thread, and move heavy work off the critical path. Debounce input and avoid synchronous layout reads.

desc.title: Improve LCP, not just bundle size
desc.description: Preload the hero image, serve modern formats, and remove render-blocking CSS. A fast server response still matters more than micro-optimisations.

desc.title: Stabilise layout
desc.description: Reserve space for images, ads, and dynamic text. CLS usually comes from late content shifting the page, not from CSS animation.

desc.title: Build a performance budget
desc.description: Set thresholds in CI for LCP, INP and CLS per route. Fail the build when a regression crosses the budget.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: Measure by route and device, fix the worst interaction first, and keep a budget. Performance is a feature you maintain.

blogList.title: FinOps for Developers: Cut Cloud Costs Without Slowing Delivery

desc.title: Cost is an engineering metric
desc.description: Cloud spend follows architecture decisions. Treat it like latency: visible, budgeted, and reviewed alongside reliability.

desc.title: Tag everything
desc.description: Require owner, environment, and service tags at provisioning. Untagged resources should be quarantined or stopped automatically.

desc.title: Right-size before optimising
desc.description: Most waste is idle capacity. Schedule non-prod shutdowns, use autoscaling, and start with smaller instances backed by metrics.

desc.title: Make storage explicit
desc.description: Set lifecycle policies for logs and backups, use tiered object storage, and delete orphaned volumes and snapshots.

desc.title: Show cost in the pull request
desc.description: Estimate infrastructure delta in CI and attach it to the PR. Engineers change behaviour when feedback arrives before deploy.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: FinOps is a loop: allocate, measure, optimise, verify. Never trade reliability for a short-term saving you cannot observe.

blogList.title: Edge and Serverless in 2026: Patterns, Costs and Hard Limits

desc.title: Choose by constraint
desc.description: Edge wins on latency near users; serverless wins on elastic burst and low operations. Neither is a default architecture.

desc.title: Keep functions small and pure
desc.description: Put business logic in testable modules and keep handlers thin. Cold starts punish huge bundles and hidden I/O.

desc.title: Design for idempotency
desc.description: Retries are normal. Use idempotency keys, durable queues, and outbox patterns so duplicate events cannot corrupt state.

desc.title: Watch the real cost curve
desc.description: Request pricing is cheap until traffic is steady and high. Compare with containers before committing to a long-lived workload.

desc.title: Plan for limits
desc.description: Execution time, memory, payload size and regional data rules shape the design. Test failure modes locally with emulators and contract tests.

desc.title: Takeaways
desc.description: Use edge for personalisation and redirects, serverless for spiky APIs, and containers for steady services. Measure before migrating.

blogList.title: Building a RAG Document Assistant with pgvector and Citations

desc.title: Start with a clear boundary
desc.description: The assistant answers only from documents uploaded by the user: PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD. It is a single-user tool with no application login or multi-tenancy, and it needs an OpenAI API key. Naming that boundary early kept the product honest: the value is grounded retrieval with visible sources, not an enterprise search platform.

desc.title: Ingestion decides answer quality
desc.description: pypdf and python-docx extract page-aware text, and RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter splits each page while keeping its exact page number. Chunks are embedded in batches of 100 with text-embedding-3-small and stored in PostgreSQL with pgvector. Format and size validation stop bad inputs before they pollute the index.

desc.title: Retrieve, then rerank
desc.description: Vector search uses an HNSW cosine index and returns 20 candidates. A structured gpt-4o-mini call scores each passage from 0 to 10, and the top 5 passages go to the answer model. If reranking fails, the pipeline falls back to vector order instead of breaking the request.

desc.title: Make grounding visible
desc.description: The answer schema contains the response and the passage numbers actually used. Sources are deduplicated by document and page, then returned with an excerpt and similarity score. When the context is insufficient, the model leaves sources empty and says the information is not in the documents.

desc.title: Build a focused interface
desc.description: The Next.js 14 UI keeps the interaction simple: upload documents, select which ones to search, ask a question and read the sources beside the answer. The FastAPI service exposes /health, document list/upload/delete and /api/chat, so the interface stays replaceable without rewriting the retrieval logic.

desc.title: Ship it like a service
desc.description: Docker Compose runs PostgreSQL/pgvector, the backend and the frontend as three services. Schema and HNSW index are created on startup, Pydantic settings validate configuration, and a documented .env template covers models, chunking, retrieval, CORS and upload limits.

desc.title: Honest next steps
desc.description: There is no dedicated evaluation dataset yet. The next iteration would add a gold question set, retrieval metrics, hybrid lexical/vector search, optional authentication for shared deployments and OCR for scanned PDFs. The current pipeline is useful precisely because its limits are explicit.

blogList.title: CommunicFlow v2: Separating the Messenger Without Rewriting the Product

desc.title: The constraint
desc.description: CommunicFlow V1 already carried the business domains: organisations, members, events, reclamations and messaging. Real-time traffic was the part that deserved its own boundary. The v2 goal was not to split everything into microservices for fashion, but to isolate the messenger so chat load, WebRTC signalling and presence would not destabilise the main REST application.

desc.title: A boundary you can deploy
desc.description: The result is a React/Vite SPA talking to an Express REST API plus a separate GraphQL/Socket.IO messenger service. GraphQL handles typed reads and mutations; Socket.IO remains the primary realtime transport. Redis backs the shared session cookie, and internal calls are authenticated with a constant-time service-key check. Three services, one clear responsibility each.

desc.title: Security is the design
desc.description: Access and refresh tokens live in HTTP-only cookies with pinned HS512 algorithms, rotation and database revocation. TOTP 2FA, backup codes and Cloudflare Turnstile cover account takeover and abusive sign-ups. A session-level active organisation and a super-admin exception make multi-tenant scope explicit instead of relying on every query to remember it.

desc.title: Realtime with rules
desc.description: The messenger provides rooms, presence, typing indicators, read receipts and bounded history pagination. Call signalling uses STUN and short-lived HMAC TURN credentials through coturn, gated by organisation policy and discussion role. This is realtime product engineering: who may see, send or call matters as much as latency.

desc.title: Business modules still matter
desc.description: v2 also added a governed Drive with access-checked serving, trash and version history, activity trail, tokenised share links and ZIP export. Events store recurrence rules and expand them at read time with a defined horizon and occurrence cap. Reclamations run through an SLA job, while notifications support preferences, grouping and realtime delivery.

desc.title: Delivery gates
desc.description: Docker Compose runs the stack behind nginx with TLS, security headers, real-IP handling and WebSocket support. A eight-stage Jenkins pipeline validates Compose config, snapshots images, polls health checks, runs smoke verification and retains rollback images. There is no Kubernetes or Prometheus stack here; the system is sized for a VPS and operated with the tools it actually has.

desc.title: What the split bought
desc.description: The messenger can fail, restart or scale without taking the core workspace down. Authentication and scope are shared deliberately, not duplicated. The hardest part was not the framework choice but keeping permissions, notifications and deployment discipline consistent across the new boundary.
